newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude may fall to $19.40 support.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude may fall to $19.40 support.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+ NYMEX crude looks weak and may fall to support levels around $19.40 a barrel on July, technical analysts said.
+ NYMEX gasoline is also weak ending under 60 cents a gallon on ACCESS on Thursday having fallen nearly eight cents in the past couple of weeks.
NYMEX crude looked likely to extend a three week downtrend when pit trading begins on Thursday, technical analysts said.
July NYMEX crude should enjoy some support just below $19.90 a barrel where it ended overnight trading on the computerised ACCESS trading system, they said.
But below the $19.80 to $19.90 area there is not much until the $19.35 to $19.45 area, said Charles Gray at brokers Prudential Bache in London.
Brokers GNI also saw the chance of a further downmove.
"On balance a move to $19.40-50 is still slightly favoured" they said in a report.

"We would have to steer clear of trading this market from the long side for the moment as products remain weak and support has not yet been secured," said brokers MeesPierson Derivatives in London, who saw possible support around the $19.72 area.
MeesPierson said "we stick to trading (heating oil) from the short side due to weakness in other markets."
July heating oil ended 0.46 cents lower at 53.70 cents a gallon on ACCESS but support was seen at 53.30 and 53.00.
MeesPierson, who specialise in market profile analysis, said gasoline had a negative "preparation" so "we continue to sell waiting either for a rally to 61.10 again or waiting for a break lower".
July gasoline ended at 59.90 cents a gallon on ACCESS on Thursday having lost nearly 8 cents a gallon over the past couple of weeks.
